prompt: It is now common for people to change careers several times during their working lives. Why is this happening? Do you think it is a positive or a negative development?
essay:
Nobody planned the end of the single-occupation career, and it is worth separating two quite different reasons for its disappearance before deciding whether to welcome it.

The first is involuntary. Automation, offshoring and the collapse of particular industries now destroy occupations faster than a working life lasts, so somebody entering the labour market at twenty can reasonably expect at least one future employer to be doing something that does not yet exist. Retraining in that situation is not an act of self-discovery; it is what happens after a redundancy notice, and calling it freedom insults the people it happens to.

The second is genuine choice, and it rests on the first. Once nobody expects a job to last, the calculation that used to keep people in unsuitable work — endure it and the pension will be there — no longer holds, and staying starts to look less prudent than moving. Cheap online qualifications made that possible in practice, allowing a second career to be prepared in the evenings rather than gambled on.

Whether the result is an improvement depends almost entirely on what surrounds it. Taken alone, mobility transfers risk from institutions to individuals: earnings drop with each restart, seniority resets, and somebody supporting a family absorbs a volatility that their employer used to carry. Taken together with portable pensions, subsidised mid-career training and a benefits system that expects periods of retraining rather than penalising them, the same mobility is straightforwardly good, because it breaks a worker's dependence on one firm and lets an economy reallocate skill without discarding the people who hold it.

My own view, then, is that this is a positive development which has been half-built. The flexibility has arrived; the institutions that would make it bearable mostly have not, and it is their absence rather than the mobility itself that people are actually complaining about.
title: Why people now change careers several times
